name: Rice

axes.label: Origin, as the sources tell it

origin.place: Several accounts; this site does not choose
origin.era: Yayoi find, Heian tonjiki, or 1885 station sale

cells.what: Cooked rice pressed by hand into a shape you can hold; called onigiri or omusubi
cells.origin: A carbonised rice lump said to be the oldest (Ishikawa, about 2,000 years ago); Heian tonjiki; first sold as a station bento in 1885
cells.regional: Local-chain rice balls (bear meat in Toyama, luncheon meat in Okinawa, scallop miso in Aomori); mehari-zushi in Wakayama
cells.know: Two onigiri days set by Nakanoto town, 18 June and 18 November; no official rule on shaping or wrapping

origin.place: India via Britain; spread through the navy

cells.what: A flour-thickened curry sauce with meat, potato, carrot and onion, served with rice
cells.origin: British curry powder arrived with recipes in early Meiji; the navy adopted curry against beriberi
cells.regional: Yokosuka navy curry (salad and milk, served in the city); Kanazawa curry (thick sauce, cabbage, steel plate); curry udon in soba shops
cells.know: Solid roux from 1950; at CoCo Ichibanya you choose the rice by weight, 300 g standard

cells.what: A large rice ball wrapped in salted takana leaves
cells.origin: A packed lunch for mountain work and between fishing trips
cells.know: Two explanations of the name; once the size of a softball
